In the [[mathematics]] of [[coding theory]], the '''Griesmer bound''', named after James Hugo Griesmer, is a bound on the length of [[Linear code|linear]] [[Binary coding|binary]] [[Block code|code]]s of dimension ''k'' and minimum distance ''d''.
There is also a very similar version for non-binary codes.

== Statement of the bound ==
For a binary linear code, the Griesmer bound is:

: <math>n\geqslant \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \left\lceil\frac{d}{2^i}\right\rceil.</math>

== Proof== 

Let <math>N(k,d)</math> denote the minimum length of a binary code of dimension ''k'' and distance ''d''. Let ''C'' be such a code. We want to show that 

:<math> N(k,d)\geqslant \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \left\lceil\frac{d}{2^i}\right\rceil.</math>

Let ''G'' be a generator matrix of ''C''. We can always suppose that the first row of ''G'' is of the form ''r''&nbsp;=&nbsp;(1,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;1,&nbsp;0,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;0) with weight ''d''.
: <math>G= \begin{bmatrix}
1 & \dots & 1 & 0 & \dots & 0 \\
\ast & \ast  & \ast &   & G' &   \\
\end{bmatrix}</math>

The matrix <math>G'</math> generates a code <math>C'</math>, which is called the residual code of <math>C.</math> <math>C'</math> obviously has dimension <math>k'=k-1</math> and length <math>n'=N(k,d)-d.</math> <math>C'</math> has a distance <math>d',</math> but we don't know it. Let <math>u\in C'</math> be such that <math>w(u)=d'</math>. There exists a vector <math>v\in \mathbb{F}_2^d</math> such that the concatenation <math>(v|u)\in C.</math> Then <math>w(v)+w(u)=w(v|u)\geqslant d.</math> On the other hand, also <math>(v|u)+r\in C,</math> since <math>r\in C</math> and <math>C</math> is linear: <math>w((v|u)+r)\geqslant d.</math> But

:<math>w((v|u)+r)=w(((1,\cdots,1)+v)|u)=d-w(v)+w(u),</math>

so this becomes <math>d-w(v)+w(u)\geqslant d</math>. By summing this with <math>w(v)+w(u)\geqslant d,</math> we obtain <math>d+2w(u)\geqslant 2d</math>. But <math>w(u)=d',</math> so we get <math>2d'\geqslant d.</math> As <math>d'</math> is integral, we get <math>d'\geqslant \left\lceil \tfrac{d}{2} \right\rceil.</math> This implies 

:<math>n'\geqslant N\left (k-1,\left\lceil \tfrac{d}{2} \right\rceil \right ),</math> 

so that

:<math>N(k,d)\geqslant d + N\left (k-1, \left\lceil \tfrac{d}{2} \right\rceil \right ).</math>

By induction over ''k'' we will eventually get 

:<math> N(k,d)\geqslant  \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \left\lceil\frac{d}{2^i}\right\rceil.</math>

Note that at any step the dimension decreases by 1 and the distance is halved, and we use the identity 

:<math>\left\lceil\frac{\left\lceil a/2^{k-1}\right\rceil}{2}\right\rceil = \left\lceil\frac{a}{2^k}\right\rceil</math> 

for any integer ''a'' and positive integer ''k''.

== Bound for the general case==
For a  linear code over <math>\mathbb{F}_q</math>, the Griesmer bound becomes:

: <math>n\geqslant \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \left\lceil\frac{d}{q^i}\right\rceil.</math>

The proof is similar to the binary case and so it is omitted.
